reflection: Name a natural material used to make one processed material.
title: Natural & Processed Materials
description: Sort twelve clearly pictured materials by whether people have manufactured or substantially changed them.
brief: Was this material found in nature, or made by substantially changing materials?

groups.label: Natural
groups.description: Found in nature in this form

items.label: Leaf
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M19 72Q13 23 80 16q4 65-52 63z" fill="#9ab982"/><path d="M22 83l48-54M37 65l-5-26M49 52l25 3"/></svg>
items.why: A leaf grows as part of a plant.

items.label: Fallen branch
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M28 22l47 21v39L28 61z" fill="#b58c62"/><ellipse cx="28" cy="42" rx="18" ry="23" fill="#e1c69f"/><ellipse cx="28" cy="42" rx="10" ry="14"/><path d="M49 45l19 9M49 59l19 9" stroke="#83634a"/></svg>

items.label: Raw cotton
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M50 88V42M50 71l-18-9M50 58l21-8" stroke="#829b71"/><path d="M24 35q-7-17 12-20 13-14 25 0 18-8 23 10 13 14-5 26-22 14-37 3-25 5-18-19z" fill="#fffdf5"/></svg>
items.why: Cotton fibres grow on cotton plants.

items.label: Raw clay
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 72q8-25 26-25-2-23 20-22 23 1 23 24 14 5 11 23z" fill="#bd8c71"/><path d="M31 67q8-12 24-9M58 40q9-7 14 3" stroke="#97694f"/></svg>
items.why: Clay is a naturally occurring earth material.

items.label: Iron ore rock
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M14 65l14-36 34-10 26 29-8 29-49 5z" fill="#9baab0"/><path d="M28 29l14 31 20-41M42 60l38 17M14 65l28-5" stroke="#6e858c"/></svg>
items.why: Iron ore is a naturally occurring rock from which iron can be extracted.

items.label: Lake water
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M24 19h52v65H24z" fill="#edf2e4"/><path d="M25 44q12-6 25 0t25 0v39H25z" fill="#8cbace"/><path d="M34 28v7" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="5"/></svg>
items.why: Lake water occurs naturally. Collecting a sample does not manufacture a new material.

items.label: Cotton fabric
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M18 17h60l7 66H23z" fill="#b9b0d5"/><path d="M30 20l4 59M46 20l4 59M62 20l4 59M21 36h59M21 52h60M22 68h61" stroke="#e5d7e4"/></svg>
items.why: People spin cotton fibres into thread and weave or knit fabric.

items.label: Paper
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M23 13h38l17 17v58H23z" fill="#fffdf5"/><path d="M61 13v17h17M33 45h32M33 57h32M33 69h20" stroke="#8bb1bd"/></svg>
items.why: People break down plant fibres and make them into paper sheets.

items.label: Fired brick
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M15 33l45-13 28 21-45 13z" fill="#df8d70"/><path d="M15 33v30l28 20V54z" fill="#b86952"/><path d="M43 54l45-13v30L43 83z" fill="#ca7b60"/></svg>
items.why: People shape clay and heat it to make bricks.

items.label: Glass cup
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M27 22h46l-6 64H33z" fill="#cbe9ef" fill-opacity=".65"/><path d="M30 22c0-7 40-7 40 0M35 32l3 40" stroke="#729aa8"/></svg>
items.why: People heat and process raw materials to make glass.

items.label: Plastic bottle
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M41 8h18v13H41z" fill="#c799ad"/><path d="M40 22q-2 15-11 18v47h42V40q-9-3-11-18z" fill="#b5d6cc"/><path d="M29 48h42M29 65h42M29 78h42"/></svg>
items.why: People manufacture plastic and mould it into a bottle.

items.label: Metal can
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="24" y="22" width="52" height="62" rx="7" fill="#b5c8cd"/><ellipse cx="50" cy="22" rx="26" ry="9" fill="#dbe4dd"/><path d="M25 45h50M25 64h50" stroke="#879fa6"/></svg>
items.why: People extract and process metal, then shape it into a can.

notes:
Focus: explain how people transform materials. Here, processed means manufactured or substantially changed. Merely picking up or collecting a natural material does not change its category.

Useful pairs: raw cotton → cotton fabric; raw clay → fired brick; plant fibres → paper; iron ore → metal objects.

This activity is separate from Natural Resources: Resource Depot. Symbols are editable inline SVG.
